Loadings plot of a PCAtools pca object

Source: R/pcaPlots.R
pcaLoadingsPlot.Rd

The interactive counterpart of PCAtools::plotloadings(). For each chosen component, the variables whose loading lies within range.retain of either end of that component's loading range are retained (PCAtools' rangeRetain rule), and every retained variable's loading is drawn on every chosen component, coloured by its value.

Usage

pcaLoadingsPlot(
  pcaobj,
  components = NULL,
  range.retain = 0.05,
  absolute = FALSE,
  low.color = "#FFD700",
  mid.color = "#FFFFFF",
  high.color = "#4169E1",
  point.size = 12,
  show.labels = TRUE,
  label.size = 10,
  main = NULL
)

Arguments

pcaobj

A PCAtools pca object.

components

Components to show, by name. Default: the first 5.

range.retain

Fraction of each component's loading range, at either end, within which variables are retained.

absolute

Logical; plot absolute loadings.

low.color, mid.color, high.color

Colour scale for negative, zero and positive loadings.

point.size

Marker size.

show.labels

Logical; label each point with its variable name.

label.size

Label font size.

main

Optional plot title.

Value

A plotly object, with the long table it draws as attribute "table".

See also

pcaLoadingsPlotServer(), PCAtools::plotloadings()

Author

Jared Andrews

Examples

data(example_pca)
pcaLoadingsPlot(example_pca, components = c("PC1", "PC2"))
